newsitem.title: USA: Neb. school $58.5 mln bond referendum rejected.
newsitem.headline: Neb. school $58.5 mln bond referendum rejected.

text.p: Voters in a fast-growing Nebraska public school district near Omaha rejected a $58.5 million bond referendum for new buildings in a special election Tuesday, the district's assistant superintendent said.

The five-year bond plan for the Papillion LaVista Public Schools would have included funds for the construction of a second high school and an eleventh elementary school in the district, Leon Dappen said.
The district had also planned to earmark some of the proceeds to renovate six of the 10 elementary schools, Dappen said.

Roughly 66 percent of the voters opposed the referendum, which could be brought before residents again in six months under Nebraska law, Dappen said. Voter turnout for the special election was roughly 23 percent of the approximately 21,000 registered voters, he added.

With the district population growing quickly, and the corresponding increase in the property tax base, the impact of the referendum on residents and businesses would have been small, Dappen said. School officials have not yet decided whether they will ask residents to consider the proposal again this year, he added.
District residents approved a $19.8 million bond referendum in 1992 for new construction and capital improvements, Dappen said.
